titulo: Repetition of indirect object pronouns (le di a Juan)
subtitulo: A mí me diste poco. Le dije a Ana la verdad.
regla: If the indirect object a + pronoun comes first in the sentence (a mí, a ella), the short pronoun is required: A mí me diste poco. With a + noun after the verb, the short pronoun is optional but very common, especially in Mexico: Le di el libro a Juan.

lista.texto: The short pronoun (**me, te, le, nos, les**) is **required**: **a ella le diste mucho**, never ~~a ella diste~~.
Optional, but very common in Mexico: **(le) di el libro a Juan**.
Required: **a Juan le di el libro**.

bloques.texto: The **a + pronoun** part alone is optional; it's for emphasis or clarity. Without it, **le** can be ambiguous (_him? her? you?_).
Tip: in Spanish the indirect object likes to be said twice.

lista.es: ==A mí me== diste muy poco dinero, pero ==a ella le== diste mucho.
lista.en: You gave me very little money, but you gave her a lot.

lista.es: ¿==A ti te== regalaron una moto tus papás?
lista.en: Did your parents give you a motorcycle?

lista.es: ==Me== diste muy poco dinero, pero ==le== diste mucho.
lista.en: You gave me very little money, but you gave him / her a lot. (unclear who)

lista.es: ==A mis papás les== mandé una postal.
lista.en: I sent my parents a postcard.

filas.t: A Juan le di el libro.
Le di el libro a Juan.

lista.nota: Both correct; the second is more common.

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: Fix it: _A nosotros dieron un premio._
lista.r: A nosotros nos dieron un premio.

lista.p: More natural: _Mandé un mensaje a mi hermana._
lista.r: Le mandé un mensaje a mi hermana.

lista.p: In Spanish (contrast): _I told HER, not him._
lista.r: Se lo dije a ella, no a él. / Le dije a ella, no a él.
